record.original_question: Let P1 be a polynomial with a periodic critical point omega of period k such that no other critical points lie in the basin of that superattracting cycle, and let P2 be a polynomial with one critical point of the same local degree, with both Julia sets connected. In the topological tuning construction, one replaces the immediate basin of omega by a copy of the dynamical plane of P2, matches external angles of P2 with internal angles of the basin, shrinks external rays of P2 to points, and makes analogous modifications at each preimage. Does this tuning construction always produce a map conjugate to a polynomial?

evidence.quote: The second type of topological surgery is tuning. First take a polynomial P1 with a periodic critical point ω of period k, and assume that no other critical points are in the entire basin of this superattractive cycle. Let P2 be a polynomial with one critical point whose degree is the same as the degree of ω. We also assume that the Julia sets of P1 and P2 are connected.
The result,P3, called P1 tuned with P2 at ω, should be conjugate to a polynomial having the same degree as P1.
Question 4. Does the tuning construction always give a result which is conjugate to a polynomial? This is true when P1 and P2 are quadratic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P1 be a complex polynomial of degree at least 2 with connected Julia set, having a superattracting periodic cycle that contains a critical point ω of period k, and such that no other critical points of P1 lie in the basin of this superattracting cycle. Let P2 be a complex polynomial with a single critical point whose local degree at that critical point equals the local degree of P1 at ω, and assume P2 also has connected Julia set.

Form a new dynamical system P3 by the following topological tuning construction: remove the immediate basin U of ω together with each strict preimage of U under iteration of P1, and into each removed component glue in a copy of the filled Julia set of P2 (the dynamical plane of P2), in such a way that the external angles of P2 are matched with the internal angles of the corresponding basin component of P1, the external rays of P2 are collapsed to points, and the gluing is performed coherently at all preimages so that the new dynamics on the modified plane extends P1 outside the basins and agrees with P2 (up to the boundary identifications) on each inserted copy.

Question: Is the resulting dynamical system P3 always topologically conjugate to a polynomial of the same degree as P1?
artifact.status_search_result: The quadratic case is classical (Douady–Hubbard). Recent work using quasiconformal surgery (e.g., Inou–Mukherjee–Shen type results, arXiv:2010.05199, 2021) has established that any primitive postcritically-finite hyperbolic polynomial can be tuned with an arbitrary generalized polynomial with non-escaping critical points, extending the Douady–Hubbard tuning theorem to higher degrees in primitive cases. The general (non-primitive, satellite) higher-degree situation is not fully settled in the same generality, so the question is best described as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Primitive tuning via quasiconformal surgery
status_evidence.snippet: Any primitive, postcritically-finite hyperbolic polynomial can be tuned with an arbitrary generalized polynomial with non-escaping critical points, generalizing a result of Douady-Hubbard for quadratic polynomials to higher degrees.
status_evidence.claim: Tuning yields a polynomial for primitive postcritically-finite hyperbolic polynomials in higher degree.

status_evidence.title: Exploring the Mandelbrot Set (Orsay Notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Douady-Hubbard tuning construction for quadratic polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: The quadratic case of the tuning construction is known to produce a polynomial.
